title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
authors: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Wojciech Tarnowski, Sergey Denisov, Karol Życzkowski
abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.
summary: This paper investigates the spectrum of random Lindblad operators that include both Hamiltonian and dissipative parts. Using advanced tools like free probability, the authors derive general equations describing how the spectral support evolves as the Hamiltonian strength changes. This is vital for understanding the dynamics of open quantum systems beyond simple dissipation.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the spectral support of random Lindblad operators, extending the analysis from purely dissipative cases to those incorporating a Hamiltonian component.
main_result: It derives a general equation for the spectral boundary, characterizing how the spectral support changes due to Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing as a function of the relative Hamiltonian strength.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques including operator-valued free probability, sequential noise averaging, and large-N limits from Random Matrix Theory.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system undergoing continuous-time Markovian evolution, governed by a Lindblad operator $L = L_H + L_D$. $L_H$ is the Hamiltonian component, and $L_D$ is the dissipative component.
key_observables: The spectral support (contour) of the Lindbladian operator $L$, and the spectral density.
important_parameters: The relative weight $\alpha$ of the Hamiltonian component, and the rank of the dissipative component.
main_assumptions: The generic case requires a novel framework combining operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging; specific normalizations are used for $K$ and $H$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the rescaled spectral support as a function of the Hamiltonian weight $\alpha$, showing lemon-like, disc, and imaginary axis supports for different $\alpha$ values.
paper_structure:

why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to analyze the spectral properties of open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding relaxation dynamics and quantum thermalization in complex physical settings.
